sources.citation: Hellenic Ministry of Culture and Sports, Odysseus portal: Archaeological site of Aphaia, Aigina (Description).
sources.quote: It is situated on the top of a hill covered with pines, in the NE part of the island, and is distinguished by the very good preservation of the Late Archaic temple. The sanctuary was initially dedicated to the cult of Aphaia, a local deity later assimilated by Athena.
sources.note: Reachable over http:// only (the https host refused connections). Further quotable line: "At the end of the period, around 500 B.C. and a little later, the sanctuary assumed the monumental form it preserves today." The page gives no dimensions and does not describe the pediments.

sources.citation: Hellenic Ministry of Culture and Sports, Odysseus portal: Archaeological site of Aphaia, Aigina (History).
sources.quote: The first systematic archaeological investigation was begun in 1901 by the German Ad. Furtwaengler. Work was resumed in 1966 by the German D. Ohly, who excavated on the site until 1979 and was continued by his collaborators until 1988.
sources.note: Reachable over http:// only. The same tab records the removal of the pediment sculptures in 1811 and their display in the Glyptothek, Munich.

sources.citation: Pausanias, Description of Greece 2.30.3, trans. W. H. S. Jones and H. A. Ormerod (Loeb Classical Library; Harvard University Press / Heinemann, 1918), via Perseus.
sources.quote: In Aegina, as you go towards the mountain of Zeus, God of all the Greeks, you reach a sanctuary of Aphaea, in whose honor Pindar composed an ode for the Aeginetans.
sources.licence: Translation published 1918 (public domain). Perseus edition: "This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 United States License." Short verbatim quotations with attribution and a link are compatible; the text is not modified.
sources.note: Licence checked on the Perseus page 2026-11-18 (CC BY-SA 3.0 US; "The Annenberg CPB/Project provided support for entering this text."). Same paragraph: Britomartis, daughter of Zeus and Carme, flees Minos into fishermen's nets and is made a goddess by Artemis; she "shows herself" in Aegina. Nothing about the architecture or the pediments.
quotes: Her surname among the Aeginetans is Aphaea; in Crete it is Dictynna (Goddess of Nets).

sources.citation: Pindar, ode composed for the Aeginetans in honour of Aphaia (lost; known through Pausanias 2.30.3).
sources.note: No text of the ode located. Furtwängler 1906 links Pindar's praise of the Aiakidai to the pediment subjects; that is interpretation, not a quotation.

sources.citation: Antoninus Liberalis, Metamorphoses 40 (Britomartis).
sources.licence: The only translation found (F. Celoria, 1992) is copyrighted: paraphrase only, never quote it in the app.
sources.note: Britomartis flees Minos to Aegina; escaping a fisherman she vanishes into a grove, and the Aeginetans call her Aphaia. The 'she who disappeared' etymology is secondary and unconfirmed.

sources.citation: Furtwängler, A., E. R. Fiechter and H. Thiersch. Aegina: Das Heiligtum der Aphaia. Munich, 1906 (text volume).
sources.licence: Public domain (1906); digitised at the Internet Archive.
sources.note: Primary source for dimensions, polychrome observations and pediment compositions. Read as archive.org OCR; page numbers are the printed running heads. Plates not seen; Heidelberg copy not opened (bot-gated).

sources.quote: The figure wears a shirt and leggings covered all over with an intricate red, yellow, blue, and green diamond pattern. Over this he wears a bright yellow vest inscribed with lions and griffins.
sources.note: On the west-pediment archer. Also: "A tall yellow hat with a flower pattern completes the costume." The curator says he "probably represents Paris".

sources.citation: Ministry of Culture and Sports, Ephorate of Antiquities of Piraeus and Islands: on-site information boards at the Sanctuary of Aphaia, Aegina: (a) 'Heiligtum der Aphaia', drawn reconstruction of the view from the approach c. 490 BC; (b) 'The area in front of the temple about 490 B.C.', aerial perspective from the north-east; (c) 'Structures and remains of buildings', plan legend 1-18. User photographs, 2026-11-18.
sources.licence: Copyrighted (Hellenic Ministry of Culture and Sports). Reference only: the photographs are not redistributed, traced or shown; only the facts read from them are used.
sources.note: Read from the user's photos (summarised in the research brief, section 21). Supersedes earlier guesses on the enclosure wall (stone socle with a mudbrick superstructure and coping, hiding the krepis from outside), the propylon (two columns in antis, central door, stair rising from the south, roof sculpture), the priests' houses (hipped tiled roofs, taller rear block, lower front block with a columned porch, pent-roof wing, against the outside of the wall), the altar (raised rear on a paved court lined with statue bases, a tall base in front), the paved way, the cistern well-head and the sphinx column (shown, attested). The Südbau is not depicted. Drawn reconstructions, not measurements: proportions taken from them are DERIVED with their own confidence.

sources.citation: SMK – Statens Museum for Kunst (National Gallery of Denmark), The Royal Cast Collection (Den Kongelige Afstøbningssamling), Copenhagen: 3D scans of plaster casts, published on SMK Open.
sources.licence: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/), as stated on each object record (field "rights"); free download without an account. Credit is given as a courtesy.
sources.note: Records read through the SMK API on 2026-11-18. Aegina casts KAS541/1-5 (east pediment; made in Munich, Technische Hochschule; acquired 1898) and KAS2123-KAS2131 (west pediment; acquired 1952). Their complete limbs show Bertel Thorvaldsen's 1816-17 restorations, removed from the Munich originals in the 1960s. KAS1800: Kore in chiton and cape (epiblema), Acropolis, c. 530 BC. No 3D files exist for the Scythian archer (KAS2130), west XIV (KAS2132), the Naxian sphinx column (KAS1462) or the Aphaia sphinx fragments (KAS1341, KAS267).

britomartis.note: Daughter of Zeus and Carme, fled Minos; worshipped in Aegina as Aphaia.

athena.note: Central figure of both pediments, unseen by the combatants (Furtwängler 1906, p. 310).

herakles.note: Helmeted archer with a lion-skin helmet front in the later east pediment (pp. 308-310). Which side he stands on is unverified.

telamon.note: With Herakles against Laomedon: the first Trojan War, subject of the later east pediment (pp. 312-314).

trojan-archer.term: Trojan archer (identified as Paris by some)
trojan-archer.note: Conflict: Furtwängler 1906 (p. 308) says the old name Paris rests on false assumptions; the 2007 Gods in Color curators say he probably represents Paris.

enclosure-wall-parapet.description: The great terrace wall rises above the terrace as an enclosure parapet: natural-stone socle 0.70 m, mudbrick 0.95 m and a tiled coping 0.15 m (overhang 0.10 m), 1.80 m in all; the east leg to the NE corner is ashlar with a flush coping; the older east stretch has its own material.
enclosure-wall-parapet.note: Construction from the Ministry board (stone socle + mudbrick + coping). Height DERIVED from the board's statement that the wall hides the krepis from outside: an eye 1.6 m above the highest approach ground outside the wall (DEM up to about 0.16 m above the terrace) needs about 1.6-1.75 m; 1.80 m chosen (tested in sanctuary-data.test.ts). Socle and coping heights conjectural. CONFLICT between the boards: the NE aerial (IMG_8187, scaled by the sphinx column's 1.45 m base slab) confirms about 1.8 m; the approach elevation (IMG_8191) draws the wall about 3.4-3.9 m above the propylon floor. User decision 2026-11-18: keep 1.8 m (the aerial).

propylon-approach-terraces.description: The approach to the propylon climbs 2.4 m over broad, low ashlar terraces running along the wall front from the fence wall to the priests' houses' rock: the top tier at the propylon floor (terrace height) carries the gate's southward projection, then seven tiers of 0.30 m (0.9 m deep) step down to the plaza; the plaza's lower south wall is flush with it.
propylon-approach-terraces.note: User decision 2026-11-20 (supersedes the two-flight stair of the same day): match the Ministry approach board (IMG_8191), whose long low courses with stepped ends let the propylon read as set into the wall line. Total climb DERIVED from the drawing (about 4 m drawn, read lower once spread over the slope; 2.4 m, +/-1 m); tier count, risers (<= 0.35 m for walking) and depths conjectural. Next to the plaza the ground is raised to at most 0.5 m below it (CONJECTURAL fill toward the board's gentle slope); the propylon floor stays at terrace height (Furtwängler p. 77); the plan footprints are kept.

priests-houses-massing.description: The SE (priests') houses outside the boundary wall: hipped tiled roofs; the rooms against the wall form a taller rear block (walls 4.2 m), rooms II-IV a lower front block (3.2 m) with the columned porch open to the west (gate side); the vestibule/forecourt a lower pent-roof wing (2.6 m).
priests-houses-massing.note: Massing and roof forms from the Ministry board; plan footprints from the digitised plan; heights and pitches DERIVED/conjectural.

site-georeference.description: The temple frame is georeferenced for the real terrain: stylobate elevation 178.14 m (DERIVED: Copernicus DEM at the OSM temple centroid minus 1 m, +/-3 m) and axis true bearing 69.1 degrees (DERIVED from the OSM outline, +/-2 degrees).
site-georeference.note: Both values are derived, not surveyed (measurements/georef.json). The sea level in the frame follows: y = -178.14.

terrain-real-beyond-terraces.description: Beyond the terrace walls the real hill and coast from the Copernicus DEM are shown; inside, the c. 490 BC terrace surfaces at Furtwängler's levels. Where today's surface rises above an ancient terrace edge, a cut face is built and the mismatch is logged.

sanctuary-phase-c490.description: The sanctuary is shown as completed c. 490 BC (Late Archaic layout); older and later structures are listed but hidden.

propylon-stairs-south.description: The propylon's flight of steps rises from the south (outer) side, as the excavator describes it and the Ministry board shows it.
propylon-stairs-south.note: RESOLVED by the Ministry on-site board (2026-11-18): the steps rise from outside, on the south. The 2007 plan's three step lines on the north (inner) side are not followed; Furtwängler pp. 75-77 (gutters draining over the stair outwards) and the board agree.

votive-column-shown.description: The sphinx votive column is shown as standing c. 490 BC: a tall single column inside the terrace carrying a marble sphinx.
votive-column-shown.note: User decision 2026-11-16 (always shown); no longer flagged uncertain since the Ministry board (2026-11-18) depicts it c. 490 BC. Height (about 10 lower diameters) and the sphinx's form remain derived/by analogy.

suedbau-shown.description: The Südbau terrace south of the sanctuary is NOT shown: listed as hidden in sanctuary.json.
suedbau-shown.note: User decision 2026-11-18 (supersedes 2026-11-16): not depicted in the Ministry reconstruction; its shape is unknown.

sanctuary-terrain.description: Terrain around the terraces is a conjectural reconstruction from the text's levels (steep fall east and north, gentle west and south, Südbau about 9 m below the stylobate), not a survey; the scan covers only the temple.

polychrome-scheme.description: Architectural colours follow what the 1906 excavators observed on Aphaia itself; the sculpture follows the Gods in Color reconstructions; gaps are filled by analogy with other Archaic temples.

black-triglyphs-and-mutules.description: Triglyphs and mutules are black, not blue: fragments found on Aphaia show black; Cockerell's blue rests on an opisthodomos piece.

dimension-baseline.description: Absolute size is anchored to the published dimensions of Furtwängler et al. 1906; the scan verifies proportions.

flank-interaxial-2-57.description: Flank interaxial 2.57 m (two text statements, pp. 24 and 55) is used over 2.56 m (p. 52 table).

corner-contraction-p29.description: Corner contraction uses the measured values on p. 29 (east 0.25 m, south 0.245 m) over the garbled p. 55 figures.

no-curvature.description: The stylobate is built level, with no curvature ("Somit ist eine Kurvatur nicht vorhanden").

east-ramp.description: A stone ramp on the east front, slope 1:6, reaching the second step and leading on to the altar.
east-ramp.note: Ramp p. 25; slope in section II.1 (page not pinned).

east-pediment-displayed.description: The later east pediment (c. 480 BC, Herakles and Telamon against Laomedon) is displayed on a c. 500 BC temple.
east-pediment-displayed.note: User decision 2026-11-16. The earlier east pediment is known only indirectly.

pediment-figure-order.description: Left-to-right figure order (west A-N, east A-L) inferred from Furtwängler's group descriptions and lettering; no single page gives it.

archer-identity.description: The painted west-pediment archer is labelled "Trojan archer (identified as Paris by some)".

pediment-scans.description: Every pediment slot shows a 3D scan of a Copenhagen plaster cast (Thorvaldsen's 1816-17 restorations as cast): a real scan of the figure, a scan mirrored from its counterpart in the mirror-symmetric composition, or a figure imagined from another scan of the same type; slots are spaced by figure height.
pediment-scans.note: User decisions 2026-11-18 (Thorvaldsen restorations accepted; mirror counterparts; imagined fills labelled). Furtwängler 1906 pp. 195, 312: mirror-symmetric groups each side of Athena.

cult-statue-standin.description: A comparable Late Archaic statue (Kore in chiton and cape from the Athenian Acropolis, c. 530 BC, Copenhagen cast) stands on the documented cult-statue base in the naos, in place of Aphaia's lost cult image.
cult-statue-standin.note: Furtwängler 1906 p. 43: base trace 92 x 112 cm at the boundary of the second third of the cella; a small, probably seated image with light-blue paint on the seat. No licensed scan of a seated Late Archaic goddess was found; a standing kore is shown instead.

sphinx-scan.description: The votive column carries a scan of a comparable sphinx (cast of the Sphinx of Aegina, c. 470-460 BC); the Aphaia original is lost, and the column's crowning sphinx is itself a restoration by analogy with the Naxian column.
sphinx-scan.note: Furtwängler 1906 pp. 157, 359-360, 487. Scaled to the 1.6 m crowning height; it faces the temple.
